scenarios.title: Read the same story in another language
scenarios.description: Named/managed Messages, opaque references, recursive grammar and captured versus live text. Sparse AI-authored French/Japanese/Arabic samples await human review; untranslated Lab content intentionally falls back to source.

checks.title: Share one Message pipeline
checks.action: Read greeting; change count; switch language in Pause / Settings.
checks.expected: Named greeting, Message Property, managed Lua and nt-tr share formatting. Live count binding refreshes without remount; causal notifications never rerun. Language review pending.

checks.title: Change recursive grammar
checks.action: Change count twice; switch English / French.
checks.expected: Count 2 selects sealed/other; 3 selects open/other with locale-formatted 1234.5. Entry exercises Lua plural-one/exact-select; native MessageRealizer tests own exhaustive CLDR categories.

checks.title: Realize an opaque reference
checks.action: Compare the two entry greeting notifications.
checks.expected: story-message realizes the same greeting as Text.msg. Arbitrary-string rejection is shared with native Lua Message-reference tests, not string-as-key authoring.

checks.title: Compare regional fallback and fonts
checks.action: Start player with fr-CA preferred; compare French / Canadian French, Japanese and Arabic in Settings.
checks.expected: Regional French inherits greeting; missing text uses source. Native labels and DejaVu/IPA font stack serve samples. Host negotiation is manual/native, not proved by launch. Human language review pending.

checks.title: Re-realize captured text and choices
checks.action: Switch during greeting reveal; Continue to Read choice, switch, then inspect Text Log.
checks.expected: Ada stays captured; Lua notifications never repeat. Choice/log use current locale. Exact locale-positioned cue crossing remains shared with native locale-cue tests and dialogue-presentation; this Scene has no voice cue.

checks.title: Replace physical image coherently
checks.action: Compare swatch in English, French and Canadian French.
checks.expected: English ui-pattern becomes magenta/teal locale-pattern in French. Canadian French explicitly uses source, stopping image inheritance while greeting still inherits.

checks.title: Keep media operation across locale commits
checks.action: Requires curated second-language Voice and distinguishable Music mapping.
checks.expected: BLOCKED: no second localized audio realization exists in Lab. Native locale-media tests protect waiter/operation identity and stale generations, not listening acceptance. Follow-up: procure, map and audition rapid switching; a notification tone is not speech.

checks.title: Preserve named-slot order in translation
checks.action: Set French, launch verbs-and-offers; begin Deliver, bind recipient then parcel; compare English and French before submit.
checks.expected: Shared Deliver template changes from Deliver {parcel} to {recipient} to À {recipient}, remettre {parcel}. Binding order remains recipient then parcel and authoritative IDs stay stable. Existing Builder UI Tests prove bindings, not locale change; word-order switch remains manual/native. AI French awaits review.

checks.title: Compare Project and engine system Messages
checks.action: Compare board Language/Resume labels and real Settings in English/French; use interaction-rules for the shared undefined-response fallback workflow.
checks.expected: Project overrides noveltea.settings.language with Language — Feature Lab / Langue — Feature Lab; Resume remains an engine Message. Board and built-in Settings share realization, no private catalog. Undefined-response fallback is intentionally shared with interaction-rules, not claimed by the label witness. AI French awaits review.

scenarios.title: Resize the reading room
scenarios.description: Canonical 1920×1080 capped-world Project, independent 1–2 UI/text settings and shared inherit/ignore samples. Immutable disabled/native policy variants remain native/build tests.

checks.title: Fit wide and tall outputs
checks.action: Resize wide/tall/HiDPI; repeat rooms-interactions wall-button/door picking at fitted edges.
checks.expected: World composition stays fixed; half-open bars reject input; targets align. Intentionally shares real pointer subjects, not caption-button surrogates. HiDPI requires suitable host.

checks.title: Separate geometry and text scale
checks.action: Settings: UI 2/text 1, UI 1/text 2, both 2; compare rulers/world landmarks.
checks.expected: Independent settings clamp to 1–2; world positions stay fixed. Ignore Mount stays unscaled. Disabled=1 and WorldOverlay behavior are shared native/immutable-Project tests. UI launch witness does not exercise shell settings.

checks.title: Compare responsive environments
checks.action: Compare inherit/ignore rulers and wide/narrow labels while changing scales and output.
checks.expected: Shared menus-and-input RCSS samples use logical media-query environments, not accidental host-DPR reflow.

checks.title: Read over enlarged world output
checks.action: Enlarge host; inspect Scene/HUD text and fitted clipping.
checks.expected: UI/ActiveText stays native-resolution over capped world. Native-world comparison remains automation-only; no in-game raster switch. Perceptual acceptance needs actual player rendering.

scenarios.title: Put the story down and return
scenarios.description: Completed deliveries, exact quantity/Location and one committed session Layout Slot contrast restore with fresh gameplay. Shell preferences/menus require a player.

checks.title: Retain old boundary during causal work
checks.action: Save delivery 1; compare manual save during shared dialogue-presentation reveal/Voice and autosave at next eligible boundary.
checks.expected: Manual writes retained candidate; autosave waits for a new eligible checkpoint. Native barrier/deferred tests own backend completion matrices; headless logical waits do not prove causal barriers.

checks.title: Restore exact authoritative state
checks.action: Save delivery 1 (quantity 3 in Inventory); Continue (quantity 2 Unplaced); load. Repeat dirty/save/load on shared properties-and-traits and runtime-workshop controls.
checks.expected: Property, quantity and Location restore without replay. Random replay shares script-and-data-flow. Trait/configuration/allocator matrices remain native; workshops provide manual state mutations, not coverage claimed by this representative Test.

checks.title: Resume exact logical continuation
checks.action: Save caption and later five-second timer; finish/load. Repeat in shared conversation-paths choice, scene-director Handoff and background-stories detached waits.
checks.expected: Completed deliveries never repeat; next Event runs once. Timer restores remaining duration. Nested/rejection matrices remain native. Shared stations' smoke Tests alone are not round-trip proofs.

checks.title: Restore intent, not DOM/VM
checks.action: Commit once, edit draft, save; commit again/load. Repeat desired actor/Material/loops in presentation-effects and sound-desk.
checks.expected: Exact Slot returns count 1; restart resets to 0. Transient draft/DOM/VM, one-shots and finite phase do not persist. Shared desired actors/loops/Materials reconstruct; audio phase restarts. UI Test asserts Slot, not audio/pixels.

checks.title: Load in current client language
checks.action: In localized-story save greeting/open choice in English; switch French, load, inspect text/choice/log.
checks.expected: Semantic Message and captured Ada restore in current preference, not saved language. No Lua replay. Shell locale changes remain manual/native; runner does not implement shell commands.

checks.title: Inspect actual saved metadata
checks.action: Pause / Save: save, overwrite with confirmation; Continue and load selected slot.
checks.expected: Metadata and fitted-game thumbnail match persisted checkpoint, not later frame. Native shell/thumbnail revision tests complement manual workflow; headless save/load proves neither confirmation nor pixels.

checks.title: Distinguish fresh gameplay from client state
checks.action: Save, commit twice and dirty deliveries; change locale/scales, pause then HUD Restart. Inspect Slot/defaults and load old slot.
checks.expected: Fresh station delivery 1/Slot 0, no implicit load; saved slots/client locale/scales survive; pause/menu stack resets. No interactive master/Purpose volume controls exist: volume persistence stays native host coverage, not per-instance gain substitution.

scenarios.title: Rooms & Interactions
scenarios.description: A reusable bedroom scene proving rejected navigation, normal Interactable/Feature interaction, state mutation, successful navigation, a Fade transition, and destination lifecycle behavior.

checks.title: Initial Room and world state
checks.action: Inspect the bedroom, door, and wall button.
checks.expected: The bedroom is current, the wall button is present and enabled, and the door begins locked.

checks.title: Locked exit rejects navigation
checks.action: Click the bedroom door while it is locked.
checks.expected: The door remains hoverable and clickable, navigation is rejected, the bedroom remains current, and the locked-door notification appears.

checks.title: Interaction mutates authored state
checks.action: Press the wall button.
checks.expected: The Interaction handles the command, sets gate-unlocked true, and emits the button notification.

checks.title: Unlocked exit navigates
checks.action: Click the bedroom door again.
checks.expected: Navigation succeeds and the destination Room becomes current.

checks.title: Non-Cut Room transition
checks.action: Watch the transition after the door opens.
checks.expected: The destination is presented through a skippable 300 ms Fade rather than an immediate Cut.

checks.title: Destination lifecycle executes
checks.action: Read the arrival notification.
checks.expected: The destination after-enter lifecycle emits its arrival notification after the Room becomes current.

checks.title: Attempted navigation and directed relocation use different guard policy
checks.action: Use the guarded policy door, then activate the Directed relocation control.
checks.guideSubtext: The door attempt stays in the workshop; the directed relocation commits to the same guarded target.
checks.expected: Ordinary navigation is vetoed by the target can-enter guard and runs rejection handling. Directed Room Change reaches the target, runs normal lifecycle, and records the guard only as a diagnostic policy condition.

scenarios.title: Room Lifecycle
scenarios.description: A compact round-trip station covering source/exit/target rejection, ordered lifecycle programs and hooks, transition context, child flow, and authored transition selection.

checks.title: Source, exit, and target rejection paths stay distinct
checks.action: Try Reject at source, Reject selected exit, and Reject at target in order.
checks.expected: Each attempt remains in the source Room and emits only the rejection handling associated with the failing phase.

checks.title: Lifecycle programs run before matching hooks
checks.action: Take Successful round trip and inspect the ordered lifecycle notifications.
checks.guideSubtext: Pre-commit programs set marker Variables; matching hooks report those markers as true.
checks.expected: Before-leave and before-enter hooks observe the immediately preceding program mutations, then after-leave and after-enter program/hook notifications occur after commit.

checks.title: Room entry context reports cause and sequence
checks.action: Complete a successful entry, then use the self-loop on the destination.
checks.expected: The after-enter hook reports navigation-attempt as the cause and a monotonically advancing entry sequence; self-entry creates a new occurrence rather than reusing the prior sequence.

checks.title: After-enter can run and resume a child flow
checks.action: From the round-trip destination choose Enter child flow and complete the Dialogue.
checks.expected: The child Room after-enter lifecycle starts the authored Dialogue, waits for it to finish, then resumes and emits the return notification without losing the Current Room.

checks.title: Lifecycle behavior at a no-Current-Room boundary
checks.action: Exercise a Room transition whose source or destination has no Current Room.
checks.expected: Only the lifecycle half applicable to the existing Room runs; there is no fabricated source or destination lifecycle.

checks.title: Room transition settings select distinct presentation
checks.action: Compare project-default Cut, Exit-level Dissolve/Fade, and an explicit requested transition.
checks.expected: Transition precedence is explicit request, selected Exit override, then project default; skipping settles at the committed destination.

scenarios.title: World Composition
scenarios.description: A camera-framed Room with duplicated Interactable occurrences, Character/Prop composition, conditional overlays, placement Layouts, world-plane ordering, and authored/runtime environments.

checks.title: Background fit remains readable under a nontrivial camera
checks.action: Activate Cycle background fit repeatedly to compare contain, cover, stretch, and center around the backdrop landmarks.
checks.expected: Cropping, bars, stretching, and centered source-image geometry change according to the selected fit while the Room camera remains zoomed and rotated.

checks.title: Occurrences stay separate from authoritative Location
checks.action: Show a Character and an Interactable at multiple placements, then move them between Room and Unplaced while independently changing visibility/eligibility.
checks.expected: Occurrences remain presentation-only: Location stays authoritative, identities are not duplicated, and hidden/disabled subjects do not bypass eligibility.

checks.title: Placement resolution follows the documented precedence
checks.action: Move an Instance through explicit dynamic placement, authored occurrence, fallback, and explicit no-presentation cases.
checks.expected: The correct occurrence is selected at each precedence level, and an ordinary move with no valid placement rejects without moving semantic Location.

checks.title: Conditions and composition hook alter one draft
checks.action: Activate either cyan sample once, then again.
checks.expected: The conditional Prop and overlay appear when enabled, while the Room compose hook independently controls the Character occurrence from the same global state; the second activation restores the initial composition.

checks.title: World planes and authored order compose predictably
checks.action: Inspect the scrolling background Environment, Interactable/Character/Prop content, and overlay Environment; compare the cross-family overlap witness in Materials & Engine2D.
checks.expected: World Background stays behind World Content, World Overlay stays above it, and local authored order controls overlap within a plane without introducing hard Prop/Interactable tiers.

checks.title: A spatial placement may mount a Layout
checks.action: Inspect the Spatial Layout marker over the center Prop.
checks.expected: The authored world-placement-marker Layout is mounted at the Prop placement and follows the placement geometry rather than behaving like a full-screen overlay.

checks.title: Room camera views respect bounds and edge policy
checks.action: Compare translated, zoomed, and rotated default/named views under bounded contain versus overscan behavior.
checks.expected: Contain clamps framing to authored bounds while overscan does not, independently of semantic Location; named-view selection and Focus require an authored invocation path before this can be completed in the Lab.

checks.title: Authored and runtime environments have explicit lifetime
checks.action: Watch both scrolling authored Environments, activate a cyan sample twice, pause/resume, then leave the Room.
checks.expected: Owner, plane, UV motion, opacity, replacement/stop-key behavior, and gameplay versus unscaled-presentation clock policies remain distinct; Room-owned environments terminate when their owner ends.

scenarios.title: Cue the stage lights
scenarios.description: Owner-qualified presentation, finite replacement, grouped Cut/Fade/Dissolve, camera emphasis, text/decorator Materials, scoped postprocess, and occurrence parameter tween/replace/skip coverage.

checks.title: Independent finite targets
checks.action: After owner/camera checks Continue: background fade, actor slide and blue-to-yellow Layout fade/swap start together; actor is immediately replaced by center fade.
checks.expected: Actor reaches complete replacement target; unrelated background/Layout operations continue. Ending Flow removes invocation intent, not saves transient phases.

checks.title: One world group, three transitions
checks.action: Continue through Cut/Fade/Dissolve; restart and skip an animated group. Open menu and resize to bars.
checks.expected: Background, actor and WorldOverlay transition together. HUD/Scene ActiveText/menu/bars remain outside world capture. Cut is immediate, Fade crosses color, Dissolve blends predecessor/target.

checks.title: Temporary shake/punch
checks.action: After visit cleanup enter the camera Dialogue; wait/advance, then restart and skip cues. Flash is intentionally shared with dialogue-presentation/timed-presentation-cue.
checks.expected: Shake/punch settle back to staged Room zoom 1.1 without altering desired framing. Awaited cues obey wait/skip. The existing pilot remains the single flash witness.

checks.title: Return, visit end and restart
checks.action: Return from owner child, then parent leaves Room. Inspect notifications and retained light/Music; restart afterward.
checks.expected: Scene actor disappears on Return, visit Prop/loop on Room leave; session Environment/loop remain until clear/restart. Semantic Test asserts public desired-state queries, not Lab pass Properties.

checks.title: Nested replacement and pagination
checks.action: Read orange/white/orange spans, then cyan page two in a shader-compiled player.
checks.expected: Inner Material replaces rather than merges outer typed float/vec4 overrides. Pagination retains visible parameters. Headless launch is not pixel proof.

checks.title: Decorator geometry and clipping
checks.action: Inspect blue WorldOverlay box, resize and change UI scale; child exceeds overflow-hidden parent.
checks.expected: Ordinary shader() Material uses renderer-owned geometry/texture and clips at the parent with premultiplied blending. No authored source replaces its reserved texture.

checks.title: Scoped replacement and stacking
checks.action: Continue World grade, Full grade, Stack, ordered inversion after/before tint, then clear. Resize to bars and compare UI/world.
checks.expected: Same grade identity moves scope; only full-game affects admitted UI, neither bars. World second effect stacks independently; reorder the noncommuting full-game tint/inversion pair to see order change. Clearing world retains full-game; clear restores original and owner end cleans remaining effects.

checks.title: Occurrence parameter tween/replace/skip
checks.action: Launch the Materials & Engine2D station; Continue into the blue tween, then replace it with the warm tween and use Fast Forward.
checks.expected: The occurrence parameter has one semantic identity: replacement supersedes the prior finite operation and skip settles the logical warm target rather than a transient interpolation value.

scenarios.title: Mix a short soundscape
scenarios.description: Desired Music/Ambience, independent one-shots, awaited completion, Voice ducking, stereo pan and pause/skip/owner cleanup. Stereo audio-enabled player required. Headless automation proves desired intent only; short Music loop awaits seam audition and runtime mix/mute controls are an explicit gap.

checks.title: Layer, replace and reconstruct loops
checks.action: Listen to Music and left/right Ambience; save/load at opening caption. Continue replaces quieter Music, clears right then all Ambience.
checks.expected: Exact identities/Purposes control replacement/clear. Load starts reconstructed loops from beginning, not decoder position. Music and SFX-backed synthetic Ambience both stream according to their Purpose; transient SFX/UI Sound use buffered playback. Semantic automation verifies logical state only.
checks.statusReason: Existing 3.318-second Music clip needs human loop-seam audition; metadata/headless playback cannot certify perceptual readiness.

checks.title: Independent one-shots and Purpose stop
checks.action: Continue after replacement: left/right one-shots overlap briefly, then fade-stop. Listen for desired loops remaining.
checks.expected: Each play is independent; same-owner transient Purpose stop leaves desired loops intact. Dialogue Voice/SFX onset remains intentionally shared with pilot.

checks.title: Actual completion versus UI Sound
checks.action: Continue Await intro; next caption appears after ordinary yielding play-and-wait/stop-and-wait. UI Sound follows without awaiting.
checks.expected: Flow resumes on actual operation completion; disposable UI Sound cannot gate gameplay. Verify in audio-enabled player, not headless elapsed-time inference.

checks.title: Preferences, gain and Voice ducking
checks.action: At Mix intro read the control gap, then Continue spoken Voice over Music with Project ducking enabled. Instance gain replacement earlier is not a master/Purpose mix control.
checks.expected: Instance gain is independent; Voice reduces Music/Ambience by configured factor then releases. Listening is required; no Property asserts mix proof.
checks.statusReason: Project Purpose volume/mute and Voice ducking settings exist, but current shell and normal Lua expose no live master/Purpose mix/mute control. Duck/release is playable; interactive mix requires an admitted runtime authoring path, not a surrogate gain flag.

checks.title: Actor/Anchor stereo bindings
checks.action: Headphones: Continue Pan intro for left Room Anchor then sliding actor under zoomed framing; compare earlier numeric pan.
checks.expected: Pan sources derive stereo position relative to Camera View; actor pan follows presentation movement. Explicit pan is independent of semantic Location, not 3D simulation.

checks.title: Pause/skip/owner cleanup
checks.action: Continue Pause intro and pause immediately; restart and skip stop/play/suppress sequence. End Flow, leave Room, restart. Visit/session loops share presentation-effects/presentation-ownership.
checks.expected: Gameplay-following and foreground-owner audio pause, unscaled continues, causal stop/play differs from disposable suppress. Flow one-shots end with owner; session Music survives Flow/Room and ends on restart. Semantic owner witness is not orphan-audio perceptual proof.
checks.statusReason: Music seam and actual host listening await acceptance.

scenarios.title: Engine2D Draw Texture & Specialization
scenarios.description: Preserved original draw-texture/specialization/order samples plus inheritance, runtime layers, Property/facet bindings, texture replacement, sampling and alpha. Continue through the guided Scene; pixel acceptance is manual, not inferred from launch automation.

checks.title: Sparse child inheritance
checks.action: Continue to inherited/strong comparison; compare the additional Prop pair without application overrides. Clear selection later to expose original applications.
checks.expected: Sparse children inherit source/renderer inputs; strength-only override changes the Prop pair. Reset reveals lower layers. Raw-image center Prop shares the ordinary preset/fallback path; editor provenance is automation-only.

checks.title: Runtime selection and parameter layers
checks.action: Continue through Layers, Away and Back; follow the caption's 0.1/0.35/0.5/0.8/1 precedence example.
checks.expected: Material-wide < authored Definition < Definition runtime < authored Instance < Instance runtime. Clearing affects one layer; switching away/back restores dormant Material-keyed values.

checks.title: Typed Property and time/size facets
checks.action: Continue through Property 0.2/0.9, occurrence-time and paint-height; pause and resize at the captions.
checks.expected: Only left occurrence follows the compatible float binding; right retains authored 0.8. Explicit clear reveals lower layers before installing another binding. Renderer-owned inputs are not writable.

checks.title: Author texture and draw sampling
checks.action: Inspect upper row: clamp-nearest, repeat-linear, repeat-inherit; third sample replaces only author-owned s_pattern with button art.
checks.expected: UVs exceed one tile: clamp smears edges, repeat tiles, nearest/linear differ on enlarged rules, inherit follows the draw image. Author substitution never replaces renderer-owned s_texColor.

checks.title: Light/dark alpha and textureless white
checks.action: Continue to Light edges and Dark edges; inspect button outlines and textureless Environment.
checks.expected: No dark fringe or double-alpha; textureless Engine2D receives neutral opaque white. Straight-alpha custom output premultiplies once; already-premultiplied postprocess/decorator inputs remain premultiplied.

checks.title: Renderer-owned draw texture is automatic
checks.action: Inspect both button sprites.
checks.guideSubtext: Both should still use the authored button image.
checks.expected: Both sprites retain the authored button image through the custom Engine2D Material even though the Material and both applications author no texture source for s_texColor.

checks.title: Definition and Instance parameter specialization
checks.action: Compare the left Definition sample with the right Instance sample.
checks.guideSubtext: The right sample should have a stronger cyan tint.
checks.expected: Both use the same Material and sprite, while the right sample has the visibly stronger cyan tint from its Instance u_strength override over the Definition value.

checks.title: WorldContent order interleaves Prop and Interactable draws
checks.action: Inspect the raw-image center Prop where it overlaps both cyan Interactable sprites.
checks.expected: The center Prop is in front of the left Interactable (orders 15 over 10) and behind the right Interactable (order 20 over 15), proving authored order interleaves draw families instead of using a hard Prop/Interactable tier.

scenarios.title: Dialogue & Presentation
scenarios.description: A compact authored Dialogue station proving normal line continuation, Character presentation changes, timed cues, audio, real choice UI, and a semantic branch consequence.

checks.title: Dialogue opens at a neutral checkpoint
checks.action: Confirm the Guide starts neutral and quiet, then continue past the ready line.
checks.guideSubtext: No presentation cue should fire before you continue.
checks.expected: The authored Dialogue opens on a neutral, cue-free ready line and requires explicit continuation before the presentation cue line begins.

checks.title: Dialogue voice cue plays after progression
checks.action: Listen when the presentation line begins.
checks.guideSubtext: The voice should start only after you leave the ready line.
checks.expected: The spoken line plays through the normal Dialogue voice path after explicit progression into the presentation line.

checks.title: Character presentation changes mid-line
checks.action: Watch the Guide during the presentation line.
checks.guideSubtext: The Guide should switch from neutral to smile partway through.
checks.expected: The Guide changes from the neutral presentation to the visibly distinct smile expression through the Dialogue cue.

checks.title: Dialogue sound-effect cue plays later
checks.action: Listen for the attention cue after the expression change.
checks.expected: The causal sound-effect cue is submitted through the normal Dialogue audio path later in the presentation line.

checks.title: Timed presentation cue fires later in reveal
checks.action: Keep watching after the expression change.
checks.guideSubtext: A brief flash should appear with the attention cue.
checks.expected: A brief skippable flash occurs at the later authored text offset without blocking normal Dialogue continuation.

checks.title: Real Dialogue choice is clickable
checks.action: When the presentation line finishes, continue to the choice and click Accept the signal.
checks.expected: The real RmlUi choice dispatches the authored Dialogue edge rather than a Lab-specific shortcut.

checks.title: Choice branch mutates authoritative state
checks.action: Choose Accept the signal and inspect the scenario state.
checks.expected: The choice edge sets presentation-accepted to true and the accepted Dialogue branch becomes active.

scenarios.title: Interview the guide
scenarios.description: Revisit a conditional transcript, unlock a disabled topic, inspect sparse presentation cues, call child Scenes, compare logging and follow completion destinations.

checks.title: Conditional transcript and stable history
checks.action: Continue the first greeting. Revisit before unlocking, then Unlock and revisit again.
checks.expected: The first greeting appears only once and interview-notes remains 1. The locked conditional line is skipped without setting interview-skipped; after unlock it appears and sets that Property to 1. Redirect returns to the same transcript, not a new invocation.

checks.title: Shown-disabled versus hidden choices
checks.action: At the first menu try the dimmed Read sealed topic, then Unlock. Later Finish into the hidden-policy conversation. Restart and Finish without unlocking to compare.
checks.expected: The first locked Read choice is visible but disabled and cannot advance. Unlock enables it. The hidden-policy optional topic is absent when locked and present when unlocked.

checks.title: Line, block and default speaker resolution
checks.action: Compare the initial Guide greeting with Inspect speakers, Stage Slots and skip cues; then read the off-screen Radio line.
checks.expected: Dialogue default Guide is used for the greeting. Block default Studio Guide overrides it for the tour, and line override Radio overrides the block. Names/colors follow the resolved Character. Only the matching speakerSync left occurrence speaks; the non-sync right and off-screen speakers do not acquire another person’s animation.

checks.title: Sparse and independent Stage Slots
checks.action: Choose Inspect speakers, Stage Slots and skip cues; continue through hide/show, smile+lean, Portrait, new Radio, clear and rebuild.
checks.expected: Hide/show retains left state; smile persists through sparse lean update. Portrait chooses close Pose; new Radio resets Character axes to stage/standing/neutral but stays left. Clear removes left; rebuild initializes defaults. Right remains unchanged throughout.

checks.title: Independent image and Character snapshot Media Slots
checks.action: Choose Inspect retained Media Slot states. Compare initial image, replacement snapshot, hide/show and clear once a Dialogue Layout realizer is available.
checks.expected: Image and Character snapshot media must be positioned by Dialogue UI independently of world actors; hide retains content and clear removes it. Current station authors the mutations but the built-in UI does not display them.
checks.statusReason: Runtime publishes media slot fields, but no built-in Media Slot image/Character-snapshot presentation exists. Complete with a normal Dialogue Layout consumer, not a world-actor surrogate.

checks.title: Ordered cues and skip barriers
checks.action: At the tour’s final line first let it reveal naturally. Restart, return to the tour and immediately skip that line.
checks.expected: Same-position smile then neutral ends neutral once. Natural reveal plays the disposable sound once; immediate skip suppresses it. The final awaited non-skippable wave is a barrier and its crossed sound is not replayed.

checks.title: Conceal and preserve child UI
checks.action: Choose Call concealed / preserved child Scenes and acknowledge each child caption.
checks.expected: Conceal removes caller text while the child owns Continue. Preserve keeps caller UI, but input still belongs to the child. Each return resumes the next exact Dialogue segment once.

checks.title: All Dialogue completion destinations
checks.action: Finish the interview, finish hidden choices, acknowledge Return and Room completion, then End the History tools.
checks.expected: Dialogue replacement enters hidden-policy once; Scene completion starts the completion tour; Return resumes the Scene at its Room-call Event; Room completion reaches Interview complete; End removes foreground Flow and keeps that Room. Handoff/ResumeDialogue is intentionally shared with scene-director/dialogue-handoff (#254), not duplicated here.

checks.title: Nested effect cursor and observable boundaries
checks.action: Unlock then Read sealed topic. Acknowledge the child caption, then read the receipt.
checks.expected: The receipt is issued and notification emitted before the child Scene. The false nested branch is skipped; after return RunLua stamps once, yielding issued / stamped. No replay duplicates the suffix.

checks.title: Admitted log entries and system append/clear
checks.action: Open Menu → History after the greeting and choices. Compare the only-choices and only-lines conversations; then Append system receipt, inspect History, Clear History and inspect again.
checks.expected: Everything keeps admitted greeting/choices with speaker/origin. OnlyChoices omits its line and any individually unlogged choice. OnlyLines omits choices and private lines. Nothing in History tools logs itself; append adds one bold system notification, clear empties the log.

scenarios.title: Dress and animate one person
scenarios.description: Two independent Character occurrences expose layered Profile/Pose/Expression/Appearance selection, automatic animation, mapped Gestures and idle clocks.

checks.title: Profiles, Poses and Expression fallback
checks.action: Continue through baseline, lean, smile and Portrait.
checks.expected: Ordered body+badge layers remain intact. Lean moves only the left base. Smile changes body art. Portrait without Pose selects close; absent Smile override uses the Profile’s default Expression composition.

checks.title: Sparse Appearance over Expression
checks.action: Compare the Hide badge and Clearing Appearance lines.
checks.expected: Appearance hides only the badge over the smiling body; clearing restores the badge while revealing unchanged underlying Expression composition.

checks.title: One shared Character, two visual occurrences
checks.action: Compare left speaker-sync and right non-sync states and read the shared-identity line.
checks.expected: Visual selection/placement axes remain independent. The studio-note Property belongs to one Studio Guide and becomes dressed; its authoritative Location remains character-studio-idles despite both Dialogue occurrences.

checks.title: Blink versus speaking precedence
checks.action: Stay on baseline and watch badges; then continue with non-speaking lines.
checks.expected: Left badge uses speaking scale pulses while matching speaker; right non-sync badge blinks on its interval. Speaking takes precedence over blink on left. Body layer remains unaffected by badge clip frames.

checks.title: Mapped Gesture completion, skip and cancellation
checks.action: Let awaited wave complete. Restart and skip the skippable wave. On Cancel gesture continue immediately before its 500 ms sound cue so the next line clears left.
checks.expected: Wave temporarily moves badge and plays its crossed cue once, then returns to desired composition. Skipped/un-crossed cues are discarded, not replayed. Clearing the target cancels its operation without modifying right.

checks.title: Reconstructible idle clocks
checks.action: Finish into Idle clocks. Compare left bob, middle sway and right pulse. Open Pause, then save/load.
checks.expected: Gameplay bob/pulse stop under pause; unscaled sway continues. After load the selected loops remain, but disposable backend phase restarts rather than resuming a saved frame.

scenarios.title: Read the illustrated notice
scenarios.description: Read styled, paged and animated text with real font faces, explicit diff emphasis, wrapped object selection and mixed Unicode scripts.

checks.title: Nested styles and real face selection
checks.action: Read the first notice line; compare nested bold/italic, underline/strike, blue, outlined, large, real versus sys synthetic faces and one-run offsets.
checks.expected: Each closing span restores its outer style. Only offset text is nudged; following text restores position. Explicit DejaVu bold/oblique use real faces while sys b/i use synthetic styling. Alpha variation is intentionally shared with text-effects/fade rather than inventing an unsupported alpha tag.

checks.title: Cluster reveal and manual/delayed paging
checks.action: Continue through manual page then delayed page; resize/enlarge text before advancing. Restart and compare immediate skip.
checks.expected: Complete é/Å clusters reveal on precomputed layout. Manual page waits for input; delayed page waits 0.6 seconds. Resize preserves current page/input boundaries and does not duplicate advancement.

checks.title: Distinct effects, waits and loops
checks.action: Observe the effect line; try skipping during its final non-skippable fade and acknowledge its wait.
checks.expected: Fade/fade-across change alpha; glow/nod/shake/tremble/pop remain distinct. Loops include authored delay/yoyo; the non-skippable effect retains its wait. Effects do not change words or duplicate Continue input.

checks.title: Wrapped semantic object selection
checks.action: Increase text scale so the long linked button phrase wraps. Hover/click the linked phrase versus plain text.
checks.expected: Only actual linked glyph/span bounds select notice-button; plain text does not select it. This is semantic subject selection, not a fake notification or a general RML button hit target.

checks.title: Explicit diff emphasis
checks.action: Read the unchanged / newly emphasized / unchanged notice.
checks.expected: Only the explicitly d-marked phrase is red/diff-emphasized; surrounding text restores normal styling. Automatic Room-description diff remains automation-only.

checks.title: Mixed-script shaping and fallback
checks.action: Read Latin combining clusters, Arabic/Hebrew with English/numbers, and CJK. Wrap, resize and enlarge text.
checks.expected: Latin clusters stay intact, RTL runs order legibly amid LTR/numbers and DejaVu supplies their glyphs; IPA Gothic supplies CJK. No tofu, corrupt wrapping or claim of color-emoji support.

scenarios.title: Operate exact objects and inventories
scenarios.description: Move exact Interactable Instances through Rooms and inventories, exercise containment and owner-qualified Features, then mutate stack quantities without losing identity semantics.

checks.title: Definition peers keep exact Instance identity
checks.action: Use Identity, then inspect Specimen A and B after A moves to Player Inventory and B becomes Unplaced.
checks.expected: Both remain distinct Instances of one Definition with their own identity-tag Property values. Room, Inventory, and Unplaced Location changes do not collapse or recreate either identity.

checks.title: Owner-qualified inventories present direct members
checks.action: Use Inventories to open the Player, Character, Interactable, Interactable Feature, and Room Feature inventories together.
checks.expected: Each view resolves the exact owner-qualified Inventory and shows only direct members; nested contents are not flattened. The current Project exercises built-in fallback presentation, while the mutually exclusive Project-default Layout branch remains blocked.
checks.statusReason: A running Project has one immutable inventory.defaultLayout setting: built-in fallback requires it to be null, while Project-default Layout resolution requires it to be non-null. The station covers all owner kinds and fallback without inventing a second project variant; complete the default/explicit/fallback matrix when Feature Lab supports per-scenario project-setting variants.

checks.title: Containment preserves direct Location and rejects cycles
checks.action: Use Containment to move the filled container to Delivery; inspect the child's direct Location and effective Room. Cycle rejection remains blocked for authored Test playback.
checks.expected: The child remains directly located in the container Inventory while its effective Room follows the moved ancestor. A containment cycle must reject atomically and leave the container in Delivery.
checks.statusReason: The station and semantic Test cover ancestor effective-Room propagation and preserved direct Inventory Location. The normal Lua move API queues a containment-cycle request, whose later atomic rejection is surfaced as an error diagnostic; authored Test playback treats any runtime error diagnostic as execution error, so it cannot currently assert that expected rejection as a passing Test without suppressing the real diagnostic.

checks.title: Enabled and visible remain independent
checks.action: Use Enabled / visible after the identity step.
checks.expected: Specimen A becomes disabled while still visible; Specimen B stays enabled while hidden in Player Inventory. Eligibility and display state do not imply one another.

checks.title: Quantity creation honors stackability and limits
checks.action: Use Create quantity to request 12 stackable supplies and quantity 2 of a non-stackable specimen.
checks.expected: Twelve supplies create the minimum three fresh stacks, each at or below limit 5 and without coalescing existing stock. Non-stackable quantity 2 creates two distinct quantity-one identities.

checks.title: Split creates identity; merge ends donor
checks.action: Use Split / merge on the four-unit Room stack.
checks.expected: Split leaves the source identity with quantity 2 and creates one quantity-2 peer inheriting Room presentation; merge restores the original receiver to 4 and ends the donor identity.

checks.title: Whole and partial exact transfers preserve the right identities
checks.action: Use Exact transfer for one whole stack and two units from another.
checks.expected: Whole transfer moves the existing identity. Partial transfer leaves the source at quantity 2 and creates exactly one quantity-2 destination identity without automatic coalescing.

checks.title: Aggregate quantity operations use stable compatible selection
checks.action: Use Aggregate on the isolated Aggregate bin.
checks.expected: Add fills compatible stacks in stable identity order, aggregate transfer splits only the boundary identity, direct totals remain exact, and consuming the exhausted source ends that identity while the surviving stock stays quantity 2.

checks.title: Invalid quantity mutations reject without partial change
checks.action: Use Rejections after Aggregate to try insufficient exact transfer and an aggregate transfer spanning incompatible stack classes.
checks.expected: Both mutations reject atomically. The exact source stays quantity 2 in its Room; aggregate pure totals can still span standard and premium classes even though an ambiguous mutating selection cannot.

checks.title: Same-named Features remain owner-qualified
checks.action: Use Feature owners to compare slot on Specimen A, Specimen B, and the Room.
checks.expected: Each same-named Feature resolves separate Properties and Inventories from its exact owner; subject identity and inventory ownership never collapse to the Feature id alone.

scenarios.title: Layer Properties and live Traits
scenarios.description: Exercise typed and schema-less Properties across exact owners, fallback precedence, runtime Trait capabilities, and recursive Conditions using effective live state.

checks.title: Typed Property values validate at runtime
checks.action: Use Typed values.
checks.expected: Boolean, integer, finite number, string, enum, and Message values resolve. Fractional integer, unknown enum, and non-finite number writes reject without replacing valid state.

checks.title: The same local key remains exact-owner scoped
checks.action: Use Owner-local.
checks.expected: shared-state changes independently on Room, Character, exact Interactable Instance, and Feature owners, including a different Character schema; Global mutation is demonstrated with global-shared-state. Exact Global/local key overlap is blocked by the runtime's project-wide Global Property namespace.
checks.statusReason: A declared Global Property ID is authoritative project-wide: identity-qualified lookup of the same key resolves it as Global and rejects the identity target. The station still exercises the same local key across Room, Character, Interactable Instance, and Feature owners plus a separate Global key; mark this ready when the runtime can represent the assigned Global/local same-key overlap.

checks.title: Override, explicit null, and unset follow fallback precedence
checks.action: Use Precedence.
checks.expected: A runtime override wins, explicit nullable null remains present, and unset reveals the next layer: Instance, Definition, Archetype, or Trait default as authored for each specimen.

checks.title: Schema-less Properties distinguish absence, null, and value
checks.action: Use Dynamic.
checks.expected: The key changes scalar type, becomes explicit null while remaining present, rejects a structural configuration that would introduce an incompatible Boolean schema, preserves prior state atomically, then returns to absence after unset.

checks.title: Live Traits add and remove capabilities without copying structure
checks.action: Use Traits to add/remove marker and Property-backed Traits and inspect the exact Instance before and after each change.
checks.expected: Trait presence and trait-value appear and disappear on the exact Instance without copying structural fields. Trait-selector dispatch and Condition evaluation must also observe runtime-added Traits.
checks.statusReason: The semantic Test covers runtime Trait add/remove and Property-backed capability resolution on the exact Instance. In aggregate authored playback, Interaction dispatch rejects a binding selected solely by that runtime-added Trait and Condition evaluation cannot reliably resolve the newly attached Trait-backed Property, so the live selector/Condition branches remain blocked until runtime authority is corrected.

checks.title: Recursive Conditions resolve mixed authoritative leaves
checks.action: Run Typed values, then use Recursive Condition.
checks.expected: All / Any / Not compose Property, Trait, exact Location, owner Inventory quantity, Lua, Current Room, and bound interaction-slot leaves; the successful rule marks conditions-hit true. Command-result lifecycle/provenance is exercised by Runtime Workshop rather than fabricated in a scope where Interaction programs do not expose sibling results.

scenarios.title: Build and mutate runtime Instances
scenarios.description: Materialize Archetypes, create compiled/effective clones, replace structural configuration, retarget a live Exit, and destroy Instances while respecting dependents.

checks.title: Archetype materialization creates independent mutable Instances
checks.action: Use Materialize.
checks.expected: Room and Character Archetypes materialize with archetype provenance. Two Character Instances keep different birth Locations, and a runtime Property written to one does not leak to its sibling.

checks.title: Runtime creation preserves source provenance and fresh identity
checks.action: Use Create / clone.
checks.expected: Rooms and Characters created from compiled/effective sources receive distinct usable IDs and compiled-definition/clone provenance; an Interactable created from its Definition starts Unplaced with a fresh identity.

checks.title: Structural configuration replacement preserves mutable world state
checks.action: Use Replace / clear.
checks.expected: Replace and clear preserve the target's Room Location and disabled state. A schema conflict and removing an Inventory with a live dependent both reject atomically; clearing returns immutable birth configuration.

checks.title: Live Exit retargeting changes ordinary Room navigation
checks.action: Use Retarget annex, then navigate through the annex Exit.
checks.expected: Ordinary Room navigation follows the live destination and arrives in Annex B. Map projection/navigation is intentionally owner-deferred for #252 and is not simulated here.

checks.title: Destruction is non-cascading and ended IDs stay ended
checks.action: Use Destroy.
checks.expected: A free Instance ends; destroying an owner with a live Inventory dependent rejects and preserves both owner and child; a later creation receives a different ID and cannot resurrect the ended identity.

scenarios.title: Discover and build named commands
scenarios.description: Exercise Primary Activate, explicit and rule-derived Offers, selector specificity and rank, discovery-versus-authority, and the built-in named-slot Command Builder.

checks.title: Primary Activate dispatches only a unique complete winner
checks.action: Activate Primary, Menu, and Ambiguous targets. Use explicit Open Verb Menu on Menu and choose an action.
checks.expected: The unique complete primary command dispatches immediately. A non-primary target requires the Verb Menu, while competing primary candidates resolve through the menu instead of guessing.

checks.title: Offer specificity, rank, and suppression are deterministic
checks.action: Activate Exact, Prefix, Trait, Definition, Feature, Rank, Rule Offer, and Suppressed targets.
checks.expected: Exact and longer qualified patterns outrank trait/definition/reusable-Feature selectors, which outrank family and any-subject. Lower rank wins equal specificity: Rank opens the Probe menu without Primary execution, then choosing Probe executes it. The rule-derived Offer participates normally, and a false winning Offer condition suppresses the Verb rather than falling through to a broader Offer.

checks.title: Discovery does not define command authority
checks.action: Compare the condition-suppressed target with a direct valid Probe command, then inspect Unavailable Probe while its availability is false.
checks.expected: The suppressed command is absent from discovery but the same fully bound valid Probe command still executes through semantic command submission. Verb availability remains the authority boundary and rejects Unavailable Probe while false.

checks.title: Named slots and bindingOrder drive command construction
checks.action: Start Deliver from the Recipient, bind the Parcel from Project Inventory, and submit through the built-in Command Builder. Also execute Deliver with the same parcel bound to both named slots.
checks.expected: bindingOrder requests recipient before parcel even though slot declaration order differs; execution binds by slot name, not position. Inventory subjects are selectable, and one live subject may legally occupy both compatible slots.

checks.title: Command Builder drafts rebind and cancel without persistence
checks.action: Begin Deliver, use Rebind on an already selected slot, choose another compatible subject, then Cancel. Repeat and leave the Room before submission; save/load around an incomplete draft if desired.
checks.expected: Rebind changes only the transient Layout-owned draft. Cancel or leaving the owning context discards the draft, and incomplete builder state is never part of save-persistent gameplay state.

checks.title: Contextual menus preserve trigger context and clamp to the viewport
checks.action: Open the Verb Menu from the near-edge Menu target with pointer input, then invoke the same subject action through non-pointer/Open Verb Menu input.
checks.expected: Pointer invocation anchors to the triggering point and clamps inside the viewport; non-pointer invocation uses the stable subject/default anchor. Menu choice continues to refer to the original triggering subject.

scenarios.title: Resolve Interaction rules and transaction boundaries
scenarios.description: Exercise live subject selectors, Guard containment tiers and priority, fallback stages, immediate atomicity, and observable command boundaries with deliberate failure controls.

checks.title: Interaction selectors resolve live subject identity
checks.action: Resolve the Character, Definition, Trait, Feature, and Exact controls, then use the runtime-created parcel placed on room entry.
checks.expected: Character family, exact Instance, owner-qualified reusable Feature, live Trait, and origin Definition selectors match the live subject. The runtime-created parcel retains its origin Definition for selector matching; no selector depends on Archetype ancestry.

checks.title: Containment tiers resolve before same-tier priority
checks.action: Run Guard tier before and after Enable guard.
checks.expected: A false narrow Guard falls through to the broader tier; once true, the narrower containment tier beats the broader rule regardless of priority. Same-tier priority and equal-winner ambiguity are intentionally shared with the focused native Interaction resolver tests so the canonical Lab remains free of deliberately ambiguous authoring diagnostics.

checks.title: Unhandled work falls through every authored fallback stage
checks.action: Invoke Fallback and inspect the final response. Compare with handled controls and the deliberate post-boundary failure.
checks.expected: No matching rule, an unhandled Verb default, and the explicit unhandled Project fallback advance in order to the localized engine response. Once handled work crosses an observable boundary, later failure does not restart fallback or replay prior effects.

checks.title: Immediate command groups commit atomically
checks.action: Invoke Atomic failure, which stages a marker mutation before an intentionally impossible exact quantity consume; then use Verify state.
checks.expected: The quantity rejection emits its real runtime diagnostic and the earlier staged marker mutation is rolled back, proving no partial commit within the immediate group.

checks.title: Observable boundaries commit prefixes and resume at the exact cursor
checks.action: Invoke Boundary failure, acknowledge its notification and child Flow, then let the nested branch reach its deliberate quantity failure. Use Verify state afterward.
checks.expected: The pre-notification and post-notification mutations commit around the observable notification boundary, the child Flow returns to the nested command cursor, and the later failure does not replay the notification/Flow or erase already committed effects.

scenarios.title: Stage a short Scene play
scenarios.description: Exercise Scene staging contexts, Scene-native text and choice, nested typed calls and outcomes, Dialogue handoff/resume, waits and Layout signals, gameplay transactions, navigation, terminal behavior, and fast-forward boundaries.

checks.title: Scene staging contexts preserve gameplay Room identity
checks.action: Run the inherited, staged-Room, and blank child Scenes at the start of the play.
checks.expected: Inherited presentation reuses the caller, staged-Room presentation borrows the authored Room without moving Current Room or admitting that Room's lifecycle/hotspots, blank staging clears presentation, and each Return restores the exact caller presentation.

checks.title: Scene Text and Choice are authoritative Scene roles
checks.action: Continue to the blue Scene Choice and select Blue.
checks.expected: The Scene-native Choice applies its authored effect, records the blue state, and branches to Scene Text without routing through Dialogue choice machinery.

checks.title: Nested Scene inputs and Outcomes stay invocation-local
checks.action: Continue into the typed child Scene and return through its Done Outcome.
checks.expected: Boolean, integer, number, explicit null, and defaulted string inputs are admitted; the child returns its declared Outcome and the exact caller resumes. Value-shape and non-leak semantics are additionally shared with focused native Scene-input execution coverage.

checks.title: Scene terminal routes preserve return ancestry
checks.action: After the main play, follow the finish-room demos for Continue Scene, Continue Dialogue, Complete Game, and ordinary release/return.
checks.expected: Return resumes the caller, Continue Scene and Continue Dialogue transfer to their authored destinations, Release to Exploration ends foreground Flow in the current Room, and Complete Game returns through the title lifecycle rather than an implicit gameplay fallthrough.

checks.title: Dialogue Handoff resumes the same suspended conversation
checks.action: Continue through both Dialogue Handoffs, using the Scene's ResumeDialogue events after each return.
checks.expected: Both handoffs return to the same calling Scene and ResumeDialogue continues the retained conversation at its exact cursor. Caller-termination discard behavior is shared with focused native Dialogue/Scene lifetime coverage rather than fabricating an authored Outcome.

checks.title: Finite events and waits preserve authored semantic order
checks.action: Use the Wait demo: let the finite background/audio work settle, continue past input wait, and observe the duration and Condition waits before the signal wait.
checks.expected: Completion dependencies, duration/input/Condition waits, and finite audio/presentation events preserve the authored semantic sequence even when visual/audio realization overlaps.

checks.title: Layout signal waits bind to the exact live Mount
checks.action: In the Wait demo, press Accept Scene signal on the mounted notice board.
checks.expected: The exact invocation-owned custom-slot Mount wakes the Scene through signal 'accepted'. Unrelated/replaced-mount rejection is intentionally shared with focused native Layout-signal lifetime coverage.

checks.title: Scene gameplay operations use ordinary atomic runtime semantics
checks.action: Finish the handoff sequence and continue through the effect batch, Interaction call, structural Exit retarget, directed Room change, and navigation attempt.
checks.expected: The exact Interactable moves, the ordinary Interaction unlocks the gate, the structural transaction retargets the live Exit, directed Room change preserves the Scene, navigation follows the retargeted Exit, and the same Scene resumes after each child operation.

checks.title: Fast-forward stops at semantic barriers
checks.action: Use the play's fast-forward control around skippable finite work, then compare Choice, non-skippable waits, and opaque Lua events.
checks.expected: State mutations execute once and skippable work settles, while Choice, non-skippable operations, and opaque Lua remain barriers. The detailed cursor/barrier matrix is intentionally shared with focused native fast-forward coverage.

scenarios.title: Run a background clock
scenarios.description: Exercise concurrent detached Scenes, deterministic duration progress, owner-scoped lifetime cleanup, and isolated background failure while foreground gameplay remains usable.

checks.title: Detached Scenes progress independently of foreground Flow
checks.action: Enter the station, leave the foreground caption open, and let the first two background clocks pass one second.
checks.expected: Foreground input remains available while two detached Scenes independently reach their waits and commit two shared-state deliveries deterministically.

checks.title: Detached owners end at their own lifetime boundaries
checks.action: Continue to end the launching Flow, leave the Room, then restart the station.
checks.expected: The flow-owned branch ends with its launching Flow, the active-room branch ends with that Room visit, runtime-session work survives both, and restart replaces the session so no old branch leaks into the fresh run.

checks.title: A background fault terminates only its branch
checks.action: Open the Background fault demo and let its broken and healthy clocks fire.
checks.expected: The broken branch emits its real runtime diagnostic and stops; the good branch and foreground continue without rewind. This deliberate runtime-error path remains manual because authored Test playback correctly treats runtime diagnostics as test failures; focused native failure-path tests provide deterministic automation.

scenarios.title: Operate a data-driven notice board
scenarios.description: Exercise public Script Modules, On Game Ready reconstruction, Room Hook Registry selection, synchronous and yielding Lua contexts, structured Data.load values, calendar APIs, saved random state, and explicit restart startup context.

checks.title: Module initialization and On Game Ready have distinct lifetimes
checks.action: Enter the station and observe the exact Room-hook notification; save at the ticket boundary, draw, load the save, and continue from the restored boundary.
checks.expected: Bootstrap imports the shared module once per VM even when requested twice and registers that same module as a Room-hook handler. On Game Ready reconstructs its transient cache from established gameplay state on the fresh VM and again on the replacement VM created by load; the hook observes that cache without a global bridge or Layout import.

checks.title: Room hooks resolve one winning selector
checks.action: Enter Script & Data, then leave through Catchall hook room.
checks.expected: The Room's direct exact before-enter hook wins over the registered catchall on entry; Inventory Workbench has no exact mapping so catchall wins there. A qualified-prefix registration is present in the same public Bootstrap registry; longest-prefix competition is intentionally shared with the focused native Hook Registry resolver test because authoring record IDs do not admit dotted qualified targets.

checks.title: Only yield-capable Lua contexts suspend
checks.action: Observe the Scene's synchronous predicate/text expression, then continue into its play-and-wait audio effect.
checks.expected: The predicate and text expression synchronously return values from established runtime state. The explicitly yield-capable effect suspends on engine-owned audio work and resumes the same Scene after completion.

checks.title: Data.load returns independent structured value trees
checks.action: Enter the station, then press Read fresh notices on its notice-board Layout.
checks.expected: Gameplay and Layout each load the declared JSON Asset through Data.load, mutate a local result, reload a fresh copy, and verify nested scalars plus explicit null object members/array slots survive without writing back to the Asset.

checks.title: Rejected Data IDs do not compromise the board
checks.action: Enter the station and inspect the handled Data-load notification.
checks.expected: A missing data ID, an image/wrong-kind ID, and a path-like ID all return handled errors through the public API; the already loaded notice board remains usable and there is no filesystem escape hatch.

checks.title: Wall-clock calendar is external to gameplay time
checks.action: Use Local / UTC calendar, pause/resume gameplay, and restart the station while comparing the displayed calendar to gameplay progress.
checks.expected: os.time/os.date expose local and UTC calendar time and os.difftime performs wall-clock arithmetic; pause/restart affects gameplay lifetime rather than controlling wall time. Deterministic clock assertions remain intentionally shared with native tests using an injected fixed clock instead of real-time sleeps.

checks.title: The deterministic random stream is save state
checks.action: Seed the ticket stream, save, draw, load, and draw again.
checks.expected: math.randomseed/math.random and noveltea.random share one deterministic session generator; the post-save draw is 21 both times, while an intentionally invalid range before each draw returns an error without consuming generator state.

checks.title: Restart creates a fresh session from copied typed startup context
checks.action: Dirty the board, optionally save slot 54, then press Restart with typed context; afterward load the saved slot if desired.
checks.expected: The Layout proves Game.startup_context returns an independent copy, then requests restart with nested boolean/integer/number/string/null/object context. The new VM begins from Project gameplay defaults and routes through that context without auto-loading prior gameplay state; save slots and user preferences remain host-owned. Save-slot persistence is observable here, while preference persistence is intentionally shared with host restart integration coverage.

scenarios.title: Assemble a reusable control panel
scenarios.description: Four typed documents and a hosted fragment demonstrate live inputs, explicit Slots and owner lifetimes. Deliberate invalid requests are opt-in; Restart recovers.

checks.title: Resolve the declared resource closure
checks.action: Inspect framed documents; Read declared Data in the fragment.
checks.expected: Shared template/stylesheet, registered image/font/data, external event Lua and dedicated Layout Lua resolve through Project namespaces. The hosted fragment uses its own event Lua. UI smoke realizes these resources rather than asserting only mount intent.

checks.title: Read typed settled bindings
checks.action: Change stock / Room label; Read bindings; Update literal / order. Invalid input is explicitly opt-in.
checks.expected: Literal, Variable, identity-Property and mode/current-Room/paused facets stay read-only and refresh after settlement. Invalid stock update is rejected at ordered validation with prior Mount intact, not inferred from the immediate queued return. Error-emitting negatives are manual/shared with native contract tests, not passing authored Tests.

checks.title: Route exact typed signals and descendants
checks.action: Continue entry Scene; Start typed signal Scene; emit from Room then Flow. Open Child Inventory and dismiss parent.
checks.expected: Only the exact Flow panel releases its receiver's accepted(count) wait. Parent dismissal removes contextual descendants. Ordinary Inventory replacement/coexistence is intentionally shared with inventory-workbench/inventory-presentation and native parent/group tests, not a second Inventory implementation.

checks.title: Separate policy updates, replacement and owner cleanup
checks.action: Edit draft; update, hide/reopen, replace visit resource, unmount/reopen; Continue, leave and revisit.
checks.expected: Compatible policy/input changes retain occurrence and draft; replacement/unmount recreate disposable UI. Flow ends on return, Visit on leave. Named-Room intent is unprojected elsewhere and returns on revisit; session survives navigation. Restart retires all. Semantic automation protects owner projection; draft/occurrence detail remains actual UI plus native lifetime tests.

checks.title: Slots outlive UI, not their scopes
checks.action: Commit each panel; unmount/reopen, leave/revisit, end Flow and restart. Save/restore at the Scene boundary.
checks.expected: Unmount preserves live Slots; Visit/Flow expire at their boundaries while Room/session hydrate later mounts. Clear restores default. Save reconstructs validated Slots in fresh occurrences, never draft/focus/Lua state. Exact scope/save matrices are shared with native Layout Slot tests; authored state assertions cannot select among multiple scope Slots for one Layout.

checks.title: Keep strict nested objects, arrays and nulls
checks.action: Commit shaped state; Read, reject extra field, Read again; Clear Slot.
checks.expected: Count, nested label/null member and number/null array positions reconstruct through the strict shape. Invalid extra field leaves prior Slot intact; Clear restores count zero/default label. Broader cycle/nonpersistable/sparse-table negatives remain native, not corrupted Lab fixtures.

checks.title: Reconstruct before first visible render
checks.action: Reopen a committed panel at narrow output; restore a save with open counters.
checks.expected: Show sees hydrated Slot/current inputs and measured dimensions; Layout.clamp_to_viewport positions before visible render, with no uninitialized count/offscreen flash. Native show/clamp and rendering checks supply deterministic geometry; no fabricated GPU checkpoint.

checks.title: Anchor immutable contextual geometry
checks.action: In Hotspots & Cursors, pick a board, inspect contextual Inventory, open child, remove that alpha/custom source and Read again.
checks.expected: Explicit Present Inventory with useTriggerAnchor transforms captured geometry into the Layout's logical space; measured anchor clamps size. Children inherit snapshot, removing the selected source does not change it, parent dismissal cascades. Separate pointer-less Scene panel uses fallback: ordinary SetLayout does not acquire a Trigger. This Inventory Layout is shared with hotspots-and-cursors. Real player pointer input verified custom-center capture, unchanged geometry after source removal, child inheritance and parent-dismissal cascade.

scenarios.title: Layer menus over the game
scenarios.description: Project pause-role replacement plus built-in shell menus, policy probes over a world button, ordinary focus controls and independent scale samples.

checks.title: Mix project and fallback system roles
checks.action: Pause / menus: visit Settings and Text Log, cancel title, Resume; later confirm title and Start.
checks.expected: Project HUD/pause and built-in title/settings/log/modal retain declarative callbacks without native magic IDs. Save/load, Builder and Scene/Dialogue roles are shared with their stations. Shell commands are unsupported in headless UI playback: manual plus native authored-role/action-gateway tests, not false UI automation.

checks.title: Separate RmlUi consumption from gameplay admission
checks.action: Open each policy probe; click blank covered world-button area and Real UI action; remove probe.
checks.expected: Normal blank space admits world but its control consumes. BlockGameplay/Modal gate world even through blank click-through space. None does not participate: world works, its controls do not; use lower Remove probe. Different planes/orders are real mounts. Actual pointer workflow plus native routing/policy tests, not direct-command proof.

checks.title: Compose independent pause sources
checks.action: Set explicit and visible Layout pause; shell Pause/Resume; remove explicit, Read pause, then remove probe.
checks.expected: Shell Resume cannot clear explicit/Layout sources. Removing explicit leaves visible Layout pause; removing last source resumes. Unscaled UI controls operate throughout; no Lab-only pause flag.

checks.title: Close only the top eligible occurrence
checks.action: Escape dismisses probe; nest Settings/confirmation over pause; Back/cancel/Escape, load or title/Start.
checks.expected: Consumed input does not reach gameplay; higher non-dismissible Modal cannot be bypassed. Back exposes underlying menu; load/title resets stack. Save portion shared with Save & Resume; native shell-stack tests cover automation while headless shell transport is unavailable.

checks.title: Focus, edit and scroll ordinary controls
checks.action: Tab/activate Focusable action, edit input, scroll to Last row; compare disabled/hidden controls.
checks.expected: Admitted keyboard activation reaches the same control-activation Property as pointer. Input draft and scrolling work; hidden/disabled controls cannot activate. No Map focus or unsupported controller/assistive claim.

checks.title: Change UI and text inheritance independently
checks.action: Mount inherit/ignore samples; change only UI then only text scale in Settings; compare ruler/text/media labels and world button.
checks.expected: Inherited screen-space samples respond independently; ignored samples remain scale 1. RCSS sees intended logical environment, not host DPR; world placement stays fixed. WorldOverlay/ActiveText comparison is shared with world-composition/active-text and #257 display; clamp/disabled-policy/HiDPI permutations stay native/Project-variant tests.

checks.title: Use the supported non-Map custom elements
checks.action: Read pause heading, HUD story text and Text Log; compare Active Text/Dialogue stations.
checks.expected: Pause realizes nt-tr; Project HUD owns its single nt-active-text; Text Log is ordinary data-bound RML, not a custom tag. ActiveText reveal/shaping is intentionally shared with active-text/dialogue-presentation; locale switching with #257. nt-map-view stays deferred.

scenarios.title: Inspect the control board
scenarios.description: Pixel occupancy versus analytic picking, conditioned semantic targets and native cursor arbitration. Contextual popups retain snapshots, not live source handles. Cursor checks require a cursor-capable host. Custom-center activation and captured Trigger lifetime have passed real player pointer checks; remaining picking/cursor permutations retain manual/native verification.

checks.title: Compare occupancy with custom rectangles
checks.action: Pick transparent left/right centers; hover opaque sides.
checks.expected: Alpha hole does not hit; custom rectangle center hits despite transparency. Side regions share one badge Feature; generated mask is correct owner union. Curated button is shared sprite-alpha witness; pattern adds a distinct hole. Real player custom-center activation passes; the prior runtime rejection did not recur. The full occupancy/hover matrix remains this manual/native workflow.

checks.title: Resolve one eligible semantic path
checks.action: Pick center, both badge sides and Room strip; toggle center and pick again; use Exit strip.
checks.expected: Owner, owner Feature, other subject, Room Feature and Exit reach ordinary semantics. Highest-order inert none never participates; conditioned center outranks owner only while eligible; sides select same badge. Picking remains pointer/manual plus native hit tests, never direct-command proof. Real player custom-owner activation passes without the previous runtime rejection; badge/condition/Room Feature/Exit permutations remain manual/native checks, not certified by that single activation.

checks.title: Keep highlights within the correct owner
checks.action: Hover/press/leave alpha/custom sides and center with alternate target off/on.
checks.expected: Default highlights use correct masks/bounds/state; left badge uses a real hotspot-overlay-custom Material, magenta when hovered and yellow when pressed. Its inherited engine bounds and owner-union mask restrict coverage. Alternate center's none policy suppresses highlight; leaving removes it without neighbor leak. Native render tests own pixel/parameter permutations.

checks.title: Arbitrate every admitted cursor source
checks.action: Compare RCSS buttons and world Hotspots; start gameplay override; set/clear Mount request, move outside UI, Continue.
checks.expected: Project default/pointer/inherited Hotspot, Definition crosshair/custom named image, RCSS auto/default/none/system/named and gameplay requests share priority/fallback. auto contributes none; clear is owner-local. Cursorless touch is not failure; forced platform rejection remains native.

checks.title: Reveal underlying cursor when the top Mount retires
checks.action: Set board wait; open upper, hide/show/unmount it; clear lower request.
checks.expected: Higher visible crosshair contributes despite Input None. Hide/unmount reveals lower Mount/session; show restores it. Clear cannot remove another owner's request; restart retires occurrences.

checks.title: Fit image cursors in the native pixel domain
checks.action: Compare RCSS small/oversized and Lua marked/oversized requests; change UI scale and compare again.
checks.expected: Declared dependencies/nearest sampling resolve both paths. RCSS hotspot is (0,0); Lua source hotspots are (4,5)/(32,40). Oversized input fits 128x128 with aspect and hotspot scaling. Native pixels do not grow with accessibility scales. Magenta marker and exact 8x counterpart are functional original art.
